rv.q: These queens rocked the entire stage with unbelievable vocals and dancing.
It's a joyous romp, educational without feeling pedantic, and crafted with such precision that it feels effortless (which, I'm sure the queens onstage would tell you, it absolutely is not ).

Directors Lucy Moss and Jamie Armitage have taken what appears on the surface to be a simple production — one set, six cast members, a small band — and made it a visually and aurally exciting experience.
SIX proves once again that this show isn’t just clever—it’s culturally fluent.
This musical about the six wives of Henry the VIII began as a student production at Cambridge, where Marlow and Moss met.
The entertainment value of “Six” is unimpeachable and the research that went into it seems pretty solid.
You will see a highly entertaining, energetic show with a relevant message that each of these women was more individually than just one of six.
But for me, the third time was simply not the charm with this overly slick production.

cn.t: Critics praise SIX as an energetic pop concert-musical that successfully reimagines Tudor history through a modern, feminist lens, with standout performances and dazzling production design making it feel more like a pop concert than traditional theater.
